title: Humble in prayer
hook: successful are the believers who are humble in their prayer and turn from idle talk (23:1–3)

segments.voice: Yesterday: masajid, last in a list of houses of prayer protected together. Your line was all houses of prayer protected.

A man walks into the mosque in Medina, prays quickly, and comes over to greet the Prophet ﷺ. The Prophet returns his greeting and says: go back and pray, for you have not prayed. The man prays again the same way, and returns. Go back and pray; you have not prayed. A third time. Finally the man says: by the One who sent you with the truth, I don't know how to do it better. Teach me. Bukhari records what he was told. Today, a new surah, Al-Mu'minun, the Believers.

The surah opens with a promise. Pickthall: "Successful indeed are the believers who are humble in their prayers". Among the first things named next is turning away from idle talk. Humble in their prayers is khashi'un, people with khushu'. It's a hard word to put in English. The Qur'an uses the same root for land lying still and lowly, waiting for rain, and for voices gone hushed before God on the Last Day. So khushu' isn't only a feeling of humility. It's a stillness, a settling, where the noise goes down and attention gathers. The man in the mosque wasn't lazy or rude. He was going fast. And the Prophet's teaching to him, in Bukhari's account, was mostly about time. Bow until you are at rest in your bowing. Rise until you're standing straight. Prostrate until you are at rest in prostration. Sit until you're at rest sitting. At rest, again and again. Not more words, not harder feelings: slower bodies. That's why the next line of the surah fits: turning from idle talk. Khushu' is hard to reach with a phone buzzing in your pocket and half a conversation still running in your head. The hurried man got three chances and then a lesson, not a scolding. Khushu' isn't a test you pass once. It's a place you return to, one position at a time.
screen: `SUCCESSFUL ARE THE HUMBLE IN PRAYER.` · `KHUSHU': STILL, HUSHED, LOWLY.` · `BOW UNTIL YOU ARE AT REST.` · `TURN FROM IDLE TALK.`

segments.voice: If you pray, take the next prayer you're due to pray, and let every position come to rest before you move to the next. If you don't, do one ordinary thing that way right now: stand slowly, sit slowly, take one breath all the way to the end. Let each part finish before the next begins.
Khushu'. Humility in prayer, a stillness where attention gathers, like land lying quiet before rain. Today's word.
Your line: not more words, slower bodies. Stillness is a place to return to. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: In the five daily prayers, Muslims are taught to pause at rest in each position, called tuma'nina, and teachers speak of khushu' as the inner stillness the outward rest is meant to support.

original.note: Arabic: khushu', humility and stillness in prayer; 23:2 calls the believers khashi'un.

trapdoor: what you thought: humble in prayer means feeling small.
what it means: a settled stillness, where the body is at rest and attention gathers.
what a scholar hears: kh-sh-' is used of lowly land (41:39) and hushed voices (20:108); the hadith of 'the one who prayed badly' (Bukhari 757) grounds the legal term tuma'nina.

chat.says: How do you get khushu' in prayer? Do I need to say more?
options: Not more words: slow down and let each position come to rest.
Yes, add extra prayers; khushu' comes from saying as much as you can.
Pray as fast as you can, so your mind has no time to wander.
chat.meaning: The Prophet taught the hurried man: bow until you are at rest, and rise, prostrate and sit at rest. Not more words; slower bodies.
